hero.title: Administration: Pallavas and Chalukyas
hero.description: A comprehensive analysis of the administrative machinery, revenue systems, and local governance during the peak of the Pallava and Badami Chalukya rule.

timeline.title: The Chronological Framework
timeline.description: The 6th to 8th century witnessed the geopolitical dominance of these two dynasties in South India.

cards.details: Pulakeshin I establishes the Badami Chalukya kingdom, replacing the Kadambas.
Narasimhavarman I (Pallava) conquers Vatapi, signifying the height of the Pallava-Chalukya struggle.
Dantidurga (Rashtrakuta) overthrows Kirtivarman II, ending the Badami Chalukya rule.

mnemonics.title: Mnemonics & Tricks
mnemonics.description: Easily recall administrative terms for the Prelims.

items.title: P-A-N-N
items.phrase: Pallava Administrative Nodes: Periyar, Ayakar, Nadu, Nagarattar
items.decryption: Use this to recall the hierarchy from smallest unit (Nagarattar/village) to the provincial level (Mandalam).

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Mistaking 'Nadu' as a purely Pallava term; it existed across most Tamil dynasties.
Assuming the administrative hierarchy was identical; Chalukyas had more centralized control compared to the Pallavas' decentralized Brahmadeya-led system.
Confusion between 'Vatapi' (Chalukya capital) and 'Kanchi' (Pallava capital) regarding administrative oversight.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Geography

  • Pallavas: Tondaimandalam (Coromandel Coast).
  • Chalukyas: Karnataka plateau and Western Deccan.

Personalities

  • Pallavas: Mahendravarman I, Narasimhavarman I.
  • Chalukyas: Pulakeshin II, Vikramaditya I.

Administrative Hierarchy

  • Pallava System:
    • Mandalam (Province) overseen by Rajakumara.
    • Kottams (Districts) managing local groups.
    • Nadus (Village clusters) governed by Nattar.
    • Sabha/Ur: Autonomous village assemblies (Brahmadeya vs. non-Brahmadeya).
  • Chalukyan System:
    • Vishayas/Rashtras: Provinces under Vishayapati.
    • Bhoga: Smaller territorial units.
    • Village level: Governed by Gramabhojaka.
FeaturePallavasChalukyas
RevenueLand tax (Kanam) + tollsBhaga and Bali (Taxes)
Local BodySabha (Control by Brahmins)Mahajanas (Village elders)
